subject: Renewal: Order form + MSA redlines for capacity expansion
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@oxbridgehealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Oxbridge Health - Procurement <procurement@oxbridgehealth.com>
Date: 2028-10-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity bump + term update

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the Q3 check-in. Oxbridge is planning to renew with Redwood and would like to: 1) move from the current 24-month term to a 36-month renewal, and 2) increase committed capacity from 2M tokens/month to 5M tokens/month (expected go-live Jan 1).

I've attached the updated order form (v3) with the capacity schedule and proposed pricing slab. Procurement has two asks up front: can you confirm Redwood is willing to 1) add Exhibit F to capture the new capacity sequencing and 2) accept proration for the partial month in Jan? Also, legal will send a redlined MSA — we prefer to circulate a single combined redline (MSA + order form) so both teams can reconcile at once.

Timeline: Oxbridge target signature window is Nov 10 — ideally we kick off redline review this week. Can you confirm a point-of-contact on your side and whether the proposed 36-month term changes any SLA/credit language?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Procurement
Oxbridge Health

Hi team — looping legal/pricing and ops.

Quick summary of asks from Oxbridge: 36-month term, capacity 2M -> 5M tokens/mo, add Exhibit F for sequencing, proration for partial January. Attached their order form v3.

Karthik: can you confirm whether moving to 36 months changes our standard SLA credit exposure (we typically hold credits constant but there are threshold carve-outs at 36+ months)?
Grace: please flag any billing/checkout ops items — we will likely need a prorated invoice for Jan and a mid-cycle capacity activation runbook. Markus: CS readiness/hand-off for Jan go-live.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Karthik/legal to review Oxbridge redline when it lands; we should aim to return a focused redline that preserves our outage credit language.
- I will prepare a clean order form with Exhibit F draft and a short mutual action plan (MAP) to keep signatures on track.

Samantha — we'll route legal redlines to Karthik today. Expect a follow-up with an internal consolidated redline by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Avery

Avery — quick read. High-level notes for negotiation: 

1) Term change (24 -> 36 months): we prefer to keep SLA/credit formulas identical; however, for multi-year commits we typically introduce a 12-month review carve-out for performance regressions. Recommend we propose: "36-month term with annual operational review; SLA credits unchanged unless materially renegotiated in review."

2) Capacity sequencing / Exhibit F: fine — ask for clear ramp dates. We'll draft Exhibit F to show staged activations and the pricing tiers mapped to those activation dates.

3) Proration: we can accept simple proration for Jan (pro-rate on days) but require the order form to include an "activation confirmation" clause from CS to gate billing.

4) Data retention & audit: Oxbridge redlines historically push more access to customer audit logs. We'll push back on any language that implies logs retention beyond contractual retention (default 90 days; enterprise customers can request extended retention as a paid add-on).

I'll draft a redline MSA (focus: clause 2.1 term, clause 6 SLA credits, clause 9 data retention) and upload to the drive. Grace/Markus — can you confirm the activation confirmation flow?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Karthik and Avery — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Attached is our legal team's consolidated MSA redline (PDF). Two items to call out: 1) they tightened the data processing section to require 180 days of retention for audit logs, and 2) they added a clause that ties price escalations to a CPI cap (they propose 2% annual cap). Procurement is flexible on Exhibit F content — they want sequencing in-month granularity.

We will need Redwood's position on retention and CPI cap before we bring in our procurement director for final sign-off. If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow (Oct 15) to walk the redline.

Best,
Samantha

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@oxbridgehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-15T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity bump + term update

Samantha — thank you, and thanks team for the quick turn.

Summary / next steps we agreed internally and will present tomorrow:
- Data retention: Redwood can offer 180-day audit log retention as a contract add-on at a modest fee; standard retention remains 90 days. We'll propose the add-on language and pricing in Exhibit F.
- CPI cap: we cannot accept an unconditional 2% annual cap across all pricing lines. Offer: 2% cap on managed service fees only (platform unit pricing remains subject to market indices). We will propose a middle path in our redline.
- SLA/credits: keep current formulas; add annual operational review window for multi-year term.
- Proration & activation: we will add an "activation confirmation" requirement from CS that gates first prorated invoice. CS (Markus/Grace) to produce a one-page activation checklist by EOD Oct 17.

Samantha — can you do the 30-minute call at 10:00 AM PT tomorrow (Oct 16)? If yes, I'll circulate a short agenda and the consolidated redline (MSA + order form + draft Exhibit F) beforehand. We'll push for a single redline exchange to get both counsel aligned.

Attachments: exhibit-f-draft.docx (docx), consolidated_redline_stub.txt (note)

Best,
Avery
